written.description: Judges an MCP server's tool definitions three ways, by YARA rule, by hosted inspection API and by asking a model, so a poisoned tool description has to clear more than one kind of reader.

alive.last_commit_message:
fix: narrow tool_poisoning.yara extracts_from_input to stop email-search false positives (#261)

$extracts_from_input paired a broad verb list (extract|parse|scan|search|
find|identify) with a broad noun list including "emails?". Searching or
finding emails is the stated core function of any mail-search/mail-list
tool (e.g. "List, search, and filter Outlook email messages"), so every
legitimate mail tool matched tool_poisoning.

Splits emails? into its own alternative with a narrower verb set
(extract|parse|scan|identify), dropping search|find. That phrasing still
reads as scraping addresses out of unrelated content, not searching a
mailbox, so real tool-poisoning attempts using that wording still fire.
